title: Xcel-funded Pano AI camera catches the Wellington fire near Breckenridge; crews hold it to one-eighth of an acre
summary: Xcel-funded Pano AI camera alerted crews to a campsite fire east of a Breckenridge neighborhood; firefighters said the early notice kept it to one-eighth of an acre (CBS Colorado, 9 July 2024).
account: CBS Colorado reported on 9 July 2024 on the Wellington fire, which broke out at an unattended campsite just east of a Breckenridge neighborhood. It was spotted by a Pano AI camera financially supported by Xcel Energy. The camera sits on a cell tower with a 360-degree view and submits an alert to emergency crews if it notices smoke. Firefighters said this was the first instance in Summit County where a wildfire was caught early thanks to the camera's early notice. It was kept to one-eighth of an acre. This followed earlier false alarms from legal campfires. Mathew Benedict of Red White and Blue Fire's Wildland Division said a location with an actual lat/long let crews drive straight to the fire. Otherwise they could spend up to an hour finding it. Xcel's Michelle Aguayo said the company had 28 Pano AI cameras installed. The fire's date is not given.
purpose: Pano AI cameras scan for smoke and alert emergency crews with a location. Catching a fire near homes early was the intended use.
deployer: Xcel Energy (camera funding); alerts received by Red White and Blue Fire
taxonomy_note: Fire spread averted is read as reduced potential for harm; Trustible's description stresses legal harm.

ratings.reason: A fire next to a residential neighborhood was kept to one-eighth of an acre. Firefighters credit the camera's early notice, though the counterfactual is their judgment.
Red White and Blue Fire received an exact location and drove straight to the fire. Benedict said locating a wildfire can otherwise take an hour.

ai_role.statement: The camera's AI smoke alert was the trigger for dispatch, according to the fire division quoted by CBS Colorado. The only source is a single local news report with named sources. The fire's date, cause of containment and any official report are not documented.

comparator.against: locating a reported wildfire without the camera's coordinates
comparator.before: the process of finding, which often time with wildfires can take an hour
comparator.after: get a location, an actual lat/long and drive straight through it
comparator.quote: It's learning Summit County and that's part of the progress, but when we can get a location, an actual lat/long and drive straight through it instead of going through the process of finding, which often time with wildfires can take an hour, just trying to figure out a location and access and figure out all the stuff and then get the troops there...it means a lot.
